101: Ships with the "frugal" personality will only use weapons that consume ammo or fuel while their health (shields + hull - the hull level when they become disabled) is at or below this percentage, or if the hostiles in the system are considerably stronger than them.
102: Determines whether the "universal ramscoop" is active on all ships. This ramscoop provides a very small amount of fuel to every ship regardless of whether it has an actual ramscoop installed. The strength of this ramscoop falls off much more strongly than normal ramscoops, requiring you to be as close to a star as possible to have any real gain in fuel. Having this enabled prevents needing to reload your save file if you run out of fuel and no NPCs spawn in the system that you can get fuel from.
103: The minimum arrival distance for all systems. Applies to both hyperdrive and jump drive travel. If the system has a defined arrival distance greater than this value, then it will be used instead. If this gamerule has a value of "(unset)", then the value defined by the system will always be used.
104: The minimum departure distance for all systems. A ship can only jump out of a system if it is farther from the system center than the departure distance. If a system has a defined departure distance greater than this value, then it will be used instead.
105: If true, then systems that do not define an arrival distance will generate one that is equal to the habitable distance of the system.
106: Note that the vanilla game does not define any arrival distances. A system without a defined arrival distance causes ships to appear near an inhabited planet, or near the system center if there is no inhabited planet.
107: If the "Habitable arrival distance" gamerule is true, systems with a habitable distance lower than this value will use this value as their arrival distance instead. If the "Minimum arrival distance" gamerule is set and is higher than this, then that will be used instead.
108: If the "Habitable arrival distance" gamerule is true, systems with a habitable distance higher than this value will use this value as their arrival distance instead.
109: A global fleet spawn rate multiplier for random fleet spawns within systems.
110: Controls whether gamerules can be altered after a pilot has been created. If true, the gamerules button will not appear on the main menu for this pilot. If you set this to true on an existing pilot, you will not be able to return to this menu after leaving.
111: Controls which carried ships (fighters and drones), when disabled, will not be hit by projectiles unless they are directly targeted. Fighters and drones are fragile ships that can be difficult and/or tedious to replace for the player, so this gamerule is a means of increasing their survivability without increasing their combat effectiveness. Disabled carried ships can still be hit by explosions, whether from weapons or exploding ships.
113: - "player": only ships owned by the player are affected.
115: Controls whether the ammo for most secondary weapons that you have installed or in your cargo will be available for purchase at any outfitter, even if that outfitter does not normally sell ammo of that type. The description of each secondary weapon will indicate whether it can be restocked anywhere when this rule is true.
116: Controls whether raid fleets are able to spawn. Raid fleets are hostile fleets that can spawn in some systems if your fleet's cargo attractiveness is much higher than its deterrence. (That is, if you have a lot of cargo space and not a lot of firepower to defend it.) If this rule is active, your fleet's raid fleet spawn chance can be viewed from the player info panel.
117: Determines whether the player can only have a limited number of escorts active at once. If active, your flagship, parked ships, and carried ships (fighters and drones) are excluded from your fleet capacity, and you will not be able to capture ships that would put you over your capacity or take off from a planet if your capacity has been reached.
118: - "none": you can have as many escorts as you want.
119: - "ship cap": you can only command up to a certain number of escorts.
120: - "crew cap": the base crew requirement of your active escorts may not exceed a certain limit.
121: - "admin cap": the limit is tied to an "administrative cost" that every ship has, with larger ships having a higher cost.
122: If the fleet size limitation is "ship cap," then this is the default maximum number of escorts that you can have active at once. This value may be increased through story events. Changing this value on an existing pilot will have no effect.
123: If the fleet size limitation is "crew cap," then this is the default maximum sum of the base required crew (i.e. excluding required crew added by outfits like turrets) across all your escorts that you can have at once. Automated ships will use a crew-equivalent value. This value may be increased through story events. Changing this value on an existing pilot will have no effect.
124: If the fleet size limitation is "admin cap," then this is the default maximum administrative capacity. Ships will have individual administrative costs that count toward your capacity. This value may be increased through story events. Changing this value on an existing pilot will have no effect.
125: Whether permadeath mode is active, and how it should behave.
126: - "lock on death": When you die, this pilot will be locked. You will be unable to load any of its saves after it enters this state, but you'll still have the save files to share and for keeping memories.
127: - "delete on death": When you die, this pilot's save files will be deleted.
128: - "lock on takeoff": When you depart from a planet, this pilot will be locked. It will be unlocked again upon landing on a planet. Forces the "Restricted save loading" gamerule to be on.
129: - "delete on takeoff": When you depart from a planet, this pilot's save file will be deleted and will only be recreated when you land. Forces the "Single save file" and "Restricted save loading" gamerules to be on.
130: If true, this pilot will only be able to have a single save file at a time. You will be unable to create snapshots and the game will not create autosaves for previous days. Only your most recent landing point will be saved.
131: If true, this pilot will be unable to reload save files while not on the safety of a planet.
132: This item is in the ship's cargo hold.
133: This item is installed on the ship. Removal may leave the ship inoperable.
